newsitem.title: UK: UK factory orders strong in only four regions - CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK factory orders strong in only four regions - CBI.

text.p: Manufacturing orders rose significantly in only four of 11 UK regions over the four months to January, a Confederation of British Industry (CBI) and Business Strategies survey said.
The survey showed a significant rise in orders among firms in the South West, Wales, West Midlands, and Northern Ireland, fell in three regions and rose marginally in four.

Manufacturers in the South West were the only ones to report a big rise in export orders, which fell in seven of 11 UK regions. The fall in export orders had an impact on manufacturers' demand in the North, but in Wales and the West Midlands where total orders rose, firms were able to offset the decline with stronger domestic orders.

Manufacturers in all regions except the North expect total new orders to rise over the coming four months, but at a slower rate than expected in October 1996. But firms in Yourshire and Humberside, the West Midlands, and the North West have raised their growth expectations since the last survey.
